title: Networks forget the old task acing the new
body: Train a network on task B after task A and performance on A often collapses, because B's updates overwrite the weights A needed. Brains mostly avoid this; networks do not by default. Continual learning research, from elastic weight consolidation to replay buffers, is the long reply to that one embarrassing asymmetry.
source_hint: McCloskey and Cohen (1989); Kirkpatrick et al. (2017)
